answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before its votes count, then randomly audit a sample of claimed work against independent evidence. If several identities coordinate to certify fabricated results, a successful audit burns their deposits and removes their influence; splitting one attacker into many names does not multiply the stake’s voting power. This makes a sybil attack costly in capital and exposes the attacker to loss, whether the fake agents gather at a wharf, tend an orchard, or ride a tide.
